correctness.rationale: Direct Gram elimination gives the orthogonal inversion map; predictor initialization reduces it to a positive Möbius orbit with |kappa|<1. Cayley linearization proves its exact formula, convergence, and branches. Parity-exact threshold inequalities and log expansion prove the sharp 1/r work constant. A skew generator with J^2=-I on the mean-zero plane gives the finite-step singular predictor and its sharp 1/|h-1| law. Exact-rational Gram tests and oscillator tests in checker.py passed. Limits for r=0, r=rho and d>=3 are distinguished.

value.rationale: The mathematical question concerns the cost and conditioning of simultaneously preserving two standard conservative invariants. Its sharp near-uniform work law and unbounded transient are realized by a concrete explicit conservative oscillator predictor at a finite step, identifying a consequential implementation boundary even though direct radial projection solves this special geometry cheaply. No global claim is made.
